drafted_from: tool:google-account-read_mail_headers's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Who sent message 18c1a2b3d4e5f888 and what is the subject? Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-read_mail_headers as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Who sent message 18c1a2b3d4e5f888 and what is the subject?" and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-read_mail_headers, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"message_id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f888"}.

3. Read what comes back: the request goes as GET  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/messages/18c1a2b3d4e5f888?format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From&metadataHeaders=To&metadataHeaders=Subject&metadataHeaders=Date.
4. Use tool:google-account-read_a_mail when you need the whole text, not the first lines.

worked_examples.title: Read who sent a Gmail message on a sample input
worked_examples.ask: Who sent message 18c1a2b3d4e5f888 and what is the subject?
worked_examples.given: read from tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (its invoke url, method and body_template) and checked against tools/read-and-write-gmail/test/rows.test.mjs. A message from sam@example.com to alex@example.com about the order pickup. The call it makes: GET the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/messages/18c1a2b3d4e5f888?format=metadata&metadataHeaders=From&metadataHeaders=To&metadataHeaders=Subject&metadataHeaders=Date.
worked_examples.hands_back: Gmail answers id "18c1a2b3d4e5f888", snippet "Your bakery order is ready at 3 PM." and payload {"headers":[{"name":"From","value":"sam@example.com"},{"name":"To","value":"alex@example.com"},{"name":"Subject","value":"Order pickup"},{"name":"Date","value":"Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:02:11 -0600"}]}.
